ECU.note: World's #1 shrimp exporter. CNA reports ~1.3 Mt of whiteleg shrimp (vannamei) exports in 2024, ~US$7bn, mostly to China, the US and the EU.

IND.note: #2 shrimp exporter (MPEDA): ~0.7 Mt of frozen shrimp exports FY2024, led by vannamei to the US and China. The US is India's largest market for peeled/value-added shrimp.

VNM.note: VASEP: ~US$4bn shrimp exports in 2024, ~0.4 Mt product weight, much value-added. Also imports raw shrimp (Ecuador/India) for reprocessing/re-export.

IDN.note: Top-5 shrimp exporter; the US is its dominant market. 2024 exports ~0.23 Mt; pressured by US price competition and anti-dumping/CVD exposure.

ARG.note: Wild red shrimp (langostino) is a major capture fishery; ~0.2 Mt exported, mainly to Spain, Italy, China, Japan and the US.

CHN.note: Largest shrimp consumer and biggest buyer of Ecuadorian shrimp (~0.7-0.8 Mt). Also farms/processes large volumes, re-exporting some. Net importer of crustaceans.

THA.note: Once the dominant shrimp exporter; output fell after EMS/disease. 2024 exports ~0.15 Mt of mostly cooked/value-added shrimp to the US, Japan, EU.

PER.note: Exports farmed vannamei (Tumbes/Piura) plus wild crustaceans; Korea, US, EU key markets. Comtrade 2024: Korea imported ~9 kt from Peru.

MEX.note: Farms vannamei (Sinaloa/Sonora) and harvests wild Gulf shrimp; the US is essentially its only export market (~15 kt in Comtrade 2024).

HND.note: Notable Central American farmed-shrimp exporter (Gulf of Fonseca); markets incl. US, EU, Mexico, Taiwan. Hit by El Nino and EU tariff competition.

SAU.note: The Gulf's largest farmed-shrimp producer (NAQUA, Red Sea). Exports vannamei to the EU, Asia, US; also supplies the domestic/GCC market.

USA.note: World's largest shrimp importer. Comtrade 2024 (HS 0306): ~710 kt imported, led by India ~246, Ecuador ~179, Indonesia ~83, Vietnam ~28 kt. Domestic Gulf/Atlantic wild harvest small (~0.1 Mt).

JPN.note: Comtrade 2024 (HS 0306): ~186 kt crustacean imports, led by India ~39, Vietnam ~25, Indonesia ~23, Russia ~20 (snow crab), Argentina ~19 kt.

KOR.note: Comtrade 2024 (HS 0306): ~130 kt crustacean imports, led by Vietnam ~39, China ~31, Russia ~19 (crab), Peru ~9 kt.

ESP.note: EU's largest shrimp/prawn market and a re-export hub. FAO/ITC: ~0.23 Mt crustacean imports from Ecuador, Argentina (langostino), Morocco. Spanish Comtrade preview rows were fragmented; FAO/ITC structural.

ITA.note: Imports ~0.11 Mt crustaceans (FAO/ITC) from Ecuador, Argentina, India, Spain; strong demand for Argentine red shrimp and vannamei.

FRA.note: Imports ~0.12 Mt shrimp/crustaceans (FAO/ITC), much cooked/peeled and re-exported within the EU; from Ecuador, India, Madagascar, intra-EU.

flows.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (US-reported, HS 0306): the US imported ~246 kt of shrimp from India — the #1 supplier, mostly peeled/value-added vannamei.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (US-reported, HS 0306): the US imported ~179 kt of shrimp from Ecuador (shell-on whiteleg).
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (US-reported, HS 0306): the US imported ~94 kt of crustaceans from Canada — cold-water shrimp, snow crab, lobster.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (US-reported, HS 0306): the US imported ~83 kt of shrimp from Indonesia (frozen vannamei).
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (US-reported, HS 0306): the US imported ~28 kt of shrimp from Vietnam, mostly value-added.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (US-reported, HS 0306): the US imported ~16 kt of wild Argentine red shrimp.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (US-reported, HS 0306): the US imported ~15 kt of shrimp from Mexico — wild Gulf and farmed vannamei.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Japan-reported, HS 0306): Japan imported ~39 kt of shrimp from India — its largest supplier.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Japan-reported, HS 0306): Japan imported ~25 kt of shrimp from Vietnam, much processed sushi/tempura product.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Japan-reported, HS 0306): Japan imported ~23 kt of shrimp from Indonesia.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Japan-reported, HS 0306): Japan imported ~20 kt of crustaceans from Russia — predominantly snow/king crab.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Japan-reported, HS 0306): Japan imported ~19 kt of wild Argentine red shrimp.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Japan-reported, HS 0306): Japan imported ~15 kt of shrimp from Ecuador (vannamei).
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Korea-reported, HS 0306): South Korea imported ~39 kt of shrimp from Vietnam — its largest supplier.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Korea-reported, HS 0306): South Korea imported ~31 kt of crustaceans from China.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Korea-reported, HS 0306): South Korea imported ~19 kt of crustaceans from Russia — largely crab.
WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 (Korea-reported, HS 0306): South Korea imported ~9 kt of shrimp from Peru (farmed vannamei).

CNA/FAO 2024: China is the largest buyer of Ecuadorian shrimp (~0.7-0.8 Mt of shell-on vannamei). China's HS 0306 partner detail is suppressed in Comtrade, so sourced from Ecuadorian export statistics.
MPEDA/FAO 2024: China is India's second-largest shrimp market (~0.1-0.15 Mt); derived from Indian export data (China partner detail suppressed).
FAO/ITC 2024: Spain is the leading EU destination for Ecuadorian shrimp (~0.08 Mt). Spanish Comtrade preview rows fragmented; FAO/ITC structural.
FAO/ITC 2024: Spain is the top market for wild Argentine red shrimp (~0.06 Mt).
FAO/ITC 2024: Italy imports ~0.03-0.04 Mt of Ecuadorian vannamei; Argentine red shrimp also popular.
FAO/ITC 2024: France imports peeled/cooked shrimp from India (~0.025 Mt).
FAO/ITC 2024: France imports ~0.02 Mt of Ecuadorian vannamei, partly via Spanish/Belgian re-export.
VASEP/FAO 2024: Vietnam imports raw shrimp (India/Ecuador) for reprocessing/re-export; ~0.08 Mt from India.
FAO/CNA 2024: Ecuador ships raw whiteleg shrimp to Vietnam (~0.04 Mt) for value-added processing and onward export.

rankings.note: Exporter rankings are FAO/national-agency 2024 product-weight figures (Ecuador CNA, India MPEDA, Vietnam VASEP). Importer rankings blend Comtrade 2024 importer-reports (USA, Japan, Korea) with FAO/ITC structural figures for China and the EU, whose HS 0306 partner detail in Comtrade is suppressed/fragmented. China is the largest single importer by volume but reports no partner breakdown.

companies.name: Thai Union Group
companies.metric: Group sales ~US$3.9bn (FY2024); one of the world's largest seafood firms.
companies.note: Major global shrimp processor and brand owner (Chicken of the Sea, John West); sources farmed shrimp across Asia and Latin America for the US and EU.
companies.improve: Should publish farm-level shrimp traceability and antibiotic/feed (fishmeal) sourcing by origin, plus volumes by species and country.

companies.name: Industrial Pesquera Santa Priscila
companies.metric: Ecuador's largest shrimp exporter; >US$1bn of vannamei exports in 2024.
companies.note: Vertically integrated Ecuadorian producer (farms, feed, processing) shipping shell-on whiteleg shrimp mainly to China, the US, the EU.
companies.improve: Should disclose mangrove-impact/water-use metrics per farm and ASC/BAP certification coverage across its supply base.

companies.name: Omarsa
companies.metric: Top-3 Ecuadorian shrimp exporter; ~US$0.6-0.8bn vannamei exports 2024.
companies.note: Family-owned exporter with strong ASC-certified volumes, supplying European retail and US importers.
companies.improve: Should publish country-by-country sales volumes and on-farm disease/antibiotic data alongside its sustainability claims.

companies.name: Avanti Feeds
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$0.7bn (FY2024); India's largest shrimp-feed maker and a major processor/exporter.
companies.note: Dominant Indian shrimp-feed supplier (JV with Thai Union) plus an integrated processing/export arm shipping vannamei to the US.
companies.improve: Should disclose feed fishmeal/fish-oil origin and the share of US-bound volume exposed to anti-dumping/CVD duties.

companies.name: High Liner Foods
companies.metric: Sales ~US$1.0bn (FY2024); leading North American frozen-seafood supplier.
companies.note: Imports and processes shrimp from Asia and Latin America for the US and Canadian markets (Sea Cuisine, FPI brands).
companies.improve: Should publish supplier-farm lists and certification coverage for its imported warm-water shrimp.

companies.name: Mowi
companies.metric: Revenue ~EUR 5.5bn (FY2024); world's largest salmon farmer with a value-added arm that includes some shrimp.
companies.note: Primarily salmon, but its consumer-products division markets shrimp/shellfish in Europe; a major diversified seafood buyer.
companies.improve: Should separately report shrimp sourcing volumes and origins within its consumer-products segment.

global.note: Global crustaceans incl. shrimp/prawns (HS 0306), kt product/live-weight. Farmed vannamei drove most growth; Ecuador's surge lifted world supply past ~9.8 Mt and traded crustaceans to ~3.95 Mt in 2024. Wild crab/lobster/cold-water shrimp make up the balance.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO/FAO envelope; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6. Farmed shrimp is among the fastest-growing aquaculture proteins; Asian/Latin American supply expansion plus rising Asian demand drive the trend, tempered by disease and feed costs.
